newsitem.title: FINLAND: Outokumpu CEO sees "good" full-97 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Outokumpu CEO sees "good" full-97 earnings.

text.p: Finnish metals and mining group Outokumpu expects that full-year earnings in 1997 will be "good", CEO Jyrki Juusela said on Thursday.
"I have been saying this spring that 1996 was hopefully a bad year between two good ones, and I think the word 'hopefully' can now be dropped," Juusela told a news conference.

He declined to specify what he meant with a good profit level, but said the group's return on investment (ROI) target was 15 percent. It was 15.7 percent in January-April compared with 5.3 percent in full-year 1996.

Outokumpu earlier reported first tertial profit before extraordinary items up 65 percent at 502 million markka ($96.9 million) and said full-year earnings would be markedly better than in 1996 when it posted a 229 million markka profit before extras and tax.
"It is hard to see how the result could crash from there, there are no horror pictures in sight," Juusela said.
Outokumpu's first tertial earnings clearly exceeded analysts' forecasts, which had been between 143 million and 303 million markka.
The strengthening dollar helped the main business area, base metals, and first tertial inventory gains surged to 226 million markka from six million in the year-ago period, Outokumpu said.
Outokumpu said world economic growth remained fairly vigorous in January-April and that growth in industrial production and investment was particularly positive.
